# Config schema

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |

| <code class="hl-key">maps</code> | <code class="hl-type">object</code> | <span class="hl-no">no</span> | — | Named, reusable key→value tables. Each entry: map_name -&gt; { key: value }. Referenced by REMAP (whole-value lookup) / REPLACE (substring) via their 'name' argument. A template may also define a same-named maps block that overrides a global entry. |
| <code class="hl-key">maps.*</code> | <code class="hl-type">object</code> | <span class="hl-no">no</span> | — | One named map. Keys and values are arbitrary strings; key order is preserved (REPLACE applies pairs in declaration order). |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates</code> | <code class="hl-type">object</code> | <span class="hl-yes">yes</span> | — | Map of template_id -&gt; broker config. Each key is a unique template identifier used with --template flag. When bxp-cli runs without --template, all templates execute in declaration order. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*</code> | <code class="hl-type">object</code> | <span class="hl-no">no</span> | — | One conversion template — see `conversion_templates.*.*` fields for contents. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.input_schema.*</code> | <code class="hl-type">expression</code> | <span class="hl-yes">yes</span> | — | Expression evaluated per input row. Result stored in the $variable. Use [ColumnName] to reference input CSV columns. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.output_schema.*</code> | <code class="hl-type">string</code> | <span class="hl-yes">yes</span> | — | $variable whose evaluated value fills this output column. Must start with $. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.row_rules.*</code> | <code class="hl-type">object</code> | <span class="hl-no">no</span> | — | One row rule. Schema-ordered children: `when` (condition), `rows` (output rows produced when matched). |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.row_rules.*.rows.*</code> | <code class="hl-type">object</code> | <span class="hl-no">no</span> | — | One output row. Map of $variable -&gt; expression overriding the value from input_schema. Empty object {} = take all values verbatim from input_schema. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.pre_pass.when</code> | <code class="hl-type">expression</code> | <span class="hl-yes">yes</span> | — | Legacy single-block form. Filter — only rows matching this condition are added to the lookup table. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.pre_pass.key</code> | <code class="hl-type">expression</code> | <span class="hl-yes">yes</span> | — | Legacy single-block form. Expression evaluated per row to produce the lookup key string. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.pre_pass.values</code> | <code class="hl-type">object</code> | <span class="hl-yes">yes</span> | — | Legacy single-block form. Map of field_name -&gt; expression. Each value is evaluated per pre-pass row and stored for retrieval via LOOKUP(key, 'field_name'). Field names have no $ prefix. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.pre_pass.values.*</code> | <code class="hl-type">expression</code> | <span class="hl-yes">yes</span> | — | Expression evaluated per pre-pass row. Result stored under the field name for LOOKUP retrieval. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.pre_pass.*</code> | <code class="hl-type">object</code> | <span class="hl-no">no</span> | — | Named pre_pass block. The map key is the block name (typed by the user in the GUI's Add-Child dialog or written directly in JSON5) and becomes part of the LOOKUP namespace; different names cannot collide. The `insert_template` below is the inner `{ when, key, values }` body — the outer `name1: { ... }` wrapper is supplied by whatever creates the entry (free-form key input in the GUI; verbatim JSON5 syntax for hand-edited configs). |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.pre_pass.*.values.*</code> | <code class="hl-type">expression</code> | <span class="hl-yes">yes</span> | — | Expression evaluated per pre-pass row. Result stored under the field name for LOOKUP retrieval. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.description</code> | <code class="hl-type">string</code> | <span class="hl-no">no</span> | — | Optional one-line summary of what this template converts, e.g. "Trading 212 -&gt; Wealthfolio". Never read by the engine; returned by template listings so a person or an agent can pick between templates. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.data_dir</code> | <code class="hl-type">string</code> | <span class="hl-yes">yes</span> | — | Path to input files, relative to this config file. e.g. "my_broker", "../data/broker", or an absolute path. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.file_type_in</code> | <code class="hl-type">string</code> | <span class="hl-no">no</span> | <code>csv</code> | Input file format. "json" reads an array-of-objects. One of: <code class="hl-str">csv</code>, <code class="hl-str">json</code>. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.file_type_out</code> | <code class="hl-type">string</code> | <span class="hl-no">no</span> | <code>csv</code> | Output file format. "json" writes an array-of-objects. One of: <code class="hl-str">csv</code>, <code class="hl-str">json</code>. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.file_pattern_in</code> | <code class="hl-type">string</code> | <span class="hl-yes">yes</span> | — | Literal suffix filter for input files in data_dir — NOT a glob. e.g. ".csv" (all), "_cash.csv" (specific suffix). A file matches when its name ends with this exact text; "*" has no special meaning. The matched suffix is also stripped to form the output filename (with file_pattern_out). |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.file_pattern_out</code> | <code class="hl-type">string</code> | <span class="hl-yes">yes</span> | — | Output filename suffix. Replaces file_pattern_in in the output filename. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.csv_header_line</code> | <code class="hl-type">number</code> | <span class="hl-no">no</span> | <code><span class="hl-num">1</span></code> | 1-based line number of the CSV header row (default 1). 0 = headerless input: no line is treated as headers, the first line is data, and columns are reachable only by position via FIELDS(n). N&gt;1 skips N-1 preamble lines. CSV input only. |

One of: <code class="hl-str">,</code>, <code class="hl-str">;</code>, <code class="hl-str">	</code>, <code class="hl-str">&#124;</code>. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.csv_delimiter_out</code> | <code class="hl-type">string</code> | <span class="hl-no">no</span> | <code>,</code> | Output CSV field separator (single character). One of: <code class="hl-str">,</code>, <code class="hl-str">;</code>, <code class="hl-str">	</code>, <code class="hl-str">&#124;</code>. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.csv_decimal_separator_in</code> | <code class="hl-type">string</code> | <span class="hl-no">no</span> | <code>.</code> | Decimal separator in input numeric fields. Set to "," for European-style CSV. Must differ from csv_delimiter_in. One of: <code class="hl-str">.</code>, <code class="hl-str">,</code>. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.csv_decimal_separator_out</code> | <code class="hl-type">string</code> | <span class="hl-no">no</span> | <code>.</code> | Decimal separator written in numeric output fields. One of: <code class="hl-str">.</code>, <code class="hl-str">,</code>. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.csv_text_quote_in</code> | <code class="hl-type">string</code> | <span class="hl-no">no</span> | <code>double</code> | Input CSV text quoting style. Use ''' in expressions for a literal single-quote. One of: <code class="hl-str">none</code>, <code class="hl-str">single</code>, <code class="hl-str">double</code>. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.csv_text_quote_out</code> | <code class="hl-type">string</code> | <span class="hl-no">no</span> | <code>none</code> | Output CSV text quoting style. One of: <code class="hl-str">none</code>, <code class="hl-str">single</code>, <code class="hl-str">double</code>. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.csv_input_encoding</code> | <code class="hl-type">string</code> | <span class="hl-no">no</span> | <code>utf-<span class="hl-num">8</span></code> | Character encoding of the input CSV file. Transcoded to UTF-8 on read. Use for legacy non-UTF-8 exports (e.g. "windows-1250" for Czech Excel). CSV only — JSON/xlsx are always UTF-8. One of: <code class="hl-str">utf-8</code>, <code class="hl-str">windows-1250</code>, <code class="hl-str">windows-1252</code>, <code class="hl-str">iso-8859-1</code>, <code class="hl-str">iso-8859-2</code>, <code class="hl-str">iso-8859-15</code>. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.csv_output_encoding</code> | <code class="hl-type">string</code> | <span class="hl-no">no</span> | <code>utf-<span class="hl-num">8</span></code> | Character encoding of the output CSV file. UTF-8 is transcoded to this code page on write; characters with no equivalent become '?'. CSV only. One of: <code class="hl-str">utf-8</code>, <code class="hl-str">windows-1250</code>, <code class="hl-str">windows-1252</code>, <code class="hl-str">iso-8859-1</code>, <code class="hl-str">iso-8859-2</code>, <code class="hl-str">iso-8859-15</code>. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.maps</code> | <code class="hl-type">object</code> | <span class="hl-no">no</span> | — | Template-local named `key→value` maps: { map_name: { key: value } }. Merged over the top-level `maps` registry (this template's entry wins on a name collision). Referenced by REMAP / REPLACE via their `'name'` argument. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.date_filter_from_filename</code> | <code class="hl-type">boolean</code> | <span class="hl-no">no</span> | <code>false</code> | When true, rows whose $date falls outside the date range encoded in the filename (YYYY-MM-DD_YYYY-MM-DD) are silently skipped. Requires $date in input_schema. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.combined_output</code> | <code class="hl-type">boolean</code> | <span class="hl-no">no</span> | <code>false</code> | When true, all input files in data_dir additionally write their rows to one merged output file '1-&lt;template_id&gt;-combined.csvx', alongside the normal per-input outputs (it is an extra file, not a replacement). Files are processed in alphabetical order so combined row order is deterministic. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.row_rules_debug_missing</code> | <code class="hl-type">boolean</code> | <span class="hl-no">no</span> | <code>false</code> | When true, rows that match no row_rules entry are printed in --debug output. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.xlsx_sheet</code> | <code class="hl-type">object</code> | <span class="hl-no">no</span> | — | When set, the xlsx file in data_dir is converted to an intermediate CSV before the normal CSV processing loop. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.zip_input</code> | <code class="hl-type">object</code> | <span class="hl-no">no</span> | — | When set, every member of each *.zip in data_dir whose name ends with entry_pattern is streamed out to a flat intermediate CSV (N per zip) before the normal CSV loop. For zipped CSV exports (e.g. RÚIAN address registry). |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.pre_pass</code> | <code class="hl-type">object</code> | <span class="hl-no">no</span> | — | First-pass lookup table(s) built before the main loop. Two accepted shapes: legacy single block `{ when, key, values }` (detected by the presence of `when`) — accessed via 2-arg `LOOKUP(key, 'field')`; or named blocks `{ name1: { when, key, values }, ... }` — each block is its own namespace, accessed via 3-arg `LOOKUP('name', key, 'field')`. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.input_schema</code> | <code class="hl-type">object</code> | <span class="hl-yes">yes</span> | — | Map of $variable -&gt; expression. Each expression is evaluated per input row. Variables are referenced in output_schema and row_rules. Iteration order does not affect results. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.output_schema</code> | <code class="hl-type">object</code> | <span class="hl-yes">yes</span> | — | Output CSV column headers mapped to $variable values. Insertion order determines column order in the output file. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.row_rules</code> | <code class="hl-type">array</code> | <span class="hl-no">no</span> | — | Ordered list of conditional routing rules. The first rule whose `when` matches produces the output rows; later rules are not evaluated. Rows matching no rule are silently skipped (or shown via row_rules_debug_missing). |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.xlsx_sheet.name</code> | <code class="hl-type">string</code> | <span class="hl-yes">yes</span> | — | Sheet name as it appears in the xlsx workbook (e.g. "CASH OPERATION"). |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.xlsx_sheet.header_row</code> | <code class="hl-type">number</code> | <span class="hl-yes">yes</span> | — | 1-based row number that contains the column headers within this sheet. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.xlsx_sheet.output_suffix</code> | <code class="hl-type">string</code> | <span class="hl-yes">yes</span> | — | Appended before ".csv" in the intermediate filename (e.g. "_3"). Use "" for no suffix. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.zip_input.entry_pattern</code> | <code class="hl-type">string</code> | <span class="hl-no">no</span> | <code>.csv</code> | Literal suffix filter for zip members to extract — NOT a glob. A member matches when its in-zip name ends with this exact text. Default ".csv". |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.zip_input.dir_mode</code> | <code class="hl-type">string</code> | <span class="hl-no">no</span> | <code>basename</code> | How a member's in-zip path becomes a flat output filename in data_dir (the CSV loop reads data_dir non-recursively). "basename" keeps the last path segment; "keep_path" replaces every '/' with path_separator (collision-safe). One of: <code class="hl-str">basename</code>, <code class="hl-str">keep_path</code>. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.zip_input.path_separator</code> | <code class="hl-type">string</code> | <span class="hl-no">no</span> | <code>_</code> | Replacement for '/' when dir_mode is "keep_path" (e.g. "CSV/x.csv" -&gt; "CSV_x.csv"). Ignored for "basename". |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.row_rules.*.when</code> | <code class="hl-type">expression</code> | <span class="hl-yes">yes</span> | — | Condition expression. Rule applies when this evaluates to truthy (non-empty, non-zero, non-"false"). |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.row_rules.*.rows</code> | <code class="hl-type">array</code> | <span class="hl-yes">yes</span> | — | Output rows produced when `when` matches. Each entry is an object overriding $variables; rows: [] silently skips the row, rows: [{}] emits one row using input_schema variables verbatim. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.pre_pass.*.when</code> | <code class="hl-type">expression</code> | <span class="hl-yes">yes</span> | — | Filter — only rows matching this condition are added to the named lookup table. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.pre_pass.*.key</code> | <code class="hl-type">expression</code> | <span class="hl-yes">yes</span> | — | Expression evaluated per row to produce the lookup key string for this named block. |
| <code class="hl-key">conversion_templates.*.pre_pass.*.values</code> | <code class="hl-type">object</code> | <span class="hl-yes">yes</span> | — | Map of field_name -&gt; expression evaluated per pre-pass row, retrieved via 3-arg LOOKUP('name', key, 'field_name'). |
